floruit.note: The year of the arrest his own life.md records off saint.gr: the four confessors «lived under the emperor Diocletian, whose reign it dates 284 to 305; they were arrested at Thessalonica in the year 304 and confessed Christ before the governor Dulcitius and the prefect Cassander». A confessor's arrest is not a death, so it is kept as a floruit.

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 16 Απριλίου εκάστου έτους», the same day as the listing. Four names in one line, so four folders. The page states one year for the arrest, 304, and none for the confessors themselves; they were not put to death but imprisoned, so there is no year of death and no `dates` object. The same page names the governor Dulcitius, before whom the three sisters Agape, Chionia and Irene were tried on this same day and in the same year; the corpus holds two other Agathons, of Rome and of the desert, and neither is this one. The page prints no hymn and no couplet.
